routing.reason: Input validation and error handling on the tasks API (POST and PATCH) plus the page's error display, with tests, so it touches back-end and front-end.
rulings: Ruling: workflow default, not direct — the fix spans the API (back) and the page (front), and AC5 (never leak internal error messages) is a security stake — cost if wrong: a slightly longer run than direct.

Ruling: skip step frame — the ticket already lists seven testable acceptance criteria, so the product owner would only repeat them — cost if wrong: an unseen edge case (e.g. a non-string title on PATCH) is found later in review.

Ruling: keep prd, architecture, ux and seo off — not a vague epic, no cross-cutting decision, no new design (only an error message shown on the page) and no public page change — cost if wrong: the error display on the page may need a small follow-up.

Ruling: security review at medium effort — input parsing and error-message disclosure are in scope, but there is no authentication, payment or personal data — cost if wrong: a subtle leak path through another error route could pass.
Ruling: plan at low effort — the work is small and well specified by the criteria — cost if wrong: the lead may under-split the tasks between back and front.

Ruling: budget $1.20 — covers plan, a back task, a front task, a review round, the security review and the visual check — cost if wrong: the run could stop before its reviews and need the user to raise it.

criteria.why: validateTitle throws 400 'title is required' for non-string/blank; called before createTask; tests cover missing, empty, blank, number, null, object.
PATCH validates title when Object.hasOwn(body,'title'); tests cover empty, blank, null, number and stored title unchanged.
Trimmed length >200 gives the specified 400 message; title returned trimmed; boundary 200/201 tested.
readJson catches JSON.parse failure and throws HttpError 400 'invalid JSON body'; tested on POST and PATCH.
fail() logs with console.error and sends generic 'internal error'; test injects a failing db and checks the secret is hidden and logged.
app.js submit handler now catches and calls show(err); api() uses body.error.
New tests cover all cases, including trim, boundaries, PATCH ordering and the 500 path.

findings.what: createServer gains an injectable `open` parameter solely for testing; small API change, but justified for the 500 test.
readJson silently turns null/array/primitive JSON bodies into {}; the ticket did not ask for it. It is documented and tested, and it avoids a TypeError 500 on body.title.
PATCH `done` is still unvalidated, so a non-boolean value could still fail in SQLite and give a 500. This is outside the ticket.
Title length is counted in UTF-16 code units, so emoji count as 2 characters. Minor.
api() now swallows a res.json() failure with .catch(() => null). It is reasonable, but it also affects successful responses, which would return null.
There is no test for the UI change (item 6). The project has no front-end test setup.

judge.summary: The diff meets all seven criteria with a small HttpError and validateTitle design, a generic 500 handler that logs the real error, and a UI catch that shows the API message. The tests are thorough, including boundary, PATCH ordering and the hidden-500 case. The only extras are minor and documented: the injectable db opener and the coercion of non-object JSON bodies to {}.
